8.47: If you are pained by any external thing, it is not this thing that disturbs you, but your own judgement about it. And it is in your power to wipe out this judgement now. But if anything in your own disposition gives you pain, who stops you from correcting your opinion? And even if you are pained because you are not doing some particular thing which seems to you to be right, why do you not act rather than complain?—But some insurmountable obstacle is in the way.—Do not be grieved, then, for the cause of its not being done does not depend on you.—But it is not worth living if this cannot be done.—Then leave life contentedly, just as a man dies who is in full activity, and well pleased, too, with the things that are obstacles.
